narrative.intro: PanTeXas Deterrence is a federal contractor with $1.6B in contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company has one award this fiscal year, making the average award size $1.6B, and obligations are down 16.3% year over year. Obligations were $13M in FY24, rose to $1.9B in FY25, and are $1.6B in FY26 to date. The reporting notes that figures are contract obligations except where individual award-value tables and expiring-contracts tables show total contract values. The single large award in FY26 dominates the vendor’s current-year obligation totals and drives the average award size. Procurement activity appears highly concentrated by award count and dollar value. That concentration matters for program stability and competitor analysis, and it frames discussions about how PanTeXas Deterrence fits into agency buying patterns and contract pipelines.

sections.heading: Who drove the big dollar swings in obligations?
sections.body: PanTeXas Deterrence’s obligations spiked to $1.9B in FY25 and then are $1.6B in FY26 to date, driven by a single large award this fiscal year. The presence of one award explains the $1.6B average award size and concentrates spending risk into that single contract. The FY24 baseline was $13M, so the vendor moved from small activity to a concentrated, high-dollar profile across FY25 and FY26 to date.
